How it works

Three steps. No account, no upload, no waiting room.

STEP 01

Add your image

Drag & drop, browse, or paste from your clipboard. JPG, PNG and WebP all work, at any size up to 5000 px. Batch mode handles a whole folder of product shots in one go.

STEP 02

The AI cuts out your subject

The RMBG-1.4 model loads once into your browser (~44 MB, then cached) and separates subject from background locally — hair, fur, glass and tricky edges included. Nothing is sent to a server.

STEP 03

Style it and download in full HD

Keep it transparent, or drop it on white, a solid color, a blurred backdrop or your own photo. Soften the edges, crop to square or passport size, trim the empty space — then download at the original resolution, free.

Passport & ID Photo Background Changer

Most passport, visa and ID applications demand a plain white (sometimes light blue or red) background — and reject photos taken against a wall at home. Take your photo anywhere, remove the background, tap the white preset, and crop to the standard 35×45 mm passport ratio with the crop chips in the tool. Your photo is never uploaded, which matters for identity documents.

  • One-tap white, light-blue and red backgrounds — the colors ID rules ask for
  • Passport 35×45 crop built into the editor
  • Private by design: ID photos stay on your device

The remove.bg alternative

Why people are switching — and why the timing matters

remove.bg has been the category’s front door for years: third-party estimates put it at roughly 105 million visits in September 2026 (Semrush estimate), and “remove bg” alone is searched about 450,000 times a month in the US (Semrush, US database). But its standalone website is closing, and its free tier was never really free at full quality.

Verified on remove.bg’s own homepage on 21 October 2026: “remove.bg’s background removal is moving to Canva. The standalone website will no longer be available from 1 December 2026 at 9:00am CET.” Accounts close, unused credits expire, the self-serve API stops, and the Canva replacement requires a Canva account — Canva’s background remover has historically been gated behind Canva Pro. Meanwhile an independent test (October 2026) found remove.bg’s free downloads limited to a 612×408 preview, with full resolution sold as paid credits.

Questions

Frequently asked questions

Is this background remover really free?+

Yes. Every removal is free, including full-resolution downloads. There are no credits, no paywall after the first image and no watermark — the AI runs on your own device, so there is no server bill to pass on to you.

Do I need to sign up or create an account?+

No. No account, no email form, no login. Open the page, drop an image, download the result. That is the whole flow.

Are my photos uploaded anywhere?+

No. The AI model (BRIA RMBG-1.4) downloads once to your browser — about 44 MB — and then runs entirely on your device using ONNX Runtime Web. Your images never leave it, which is why this tool is a safe choice for personal ID and passport photos.

What resolution do I get back?+

Your image comes back at its original resolution, up to 5000 px on the longest side. Nothing is downscaled — unlike remove.bg’s free tier, which an independent test in October 2026 found limited to a 612×408 preview.

What is happening to remove.bg?+

remove.bg announced on its own homepage that its background removal is moving to Canva and the standalone website will no longer be available from 1 December 2026 at 9:00am CET. Accounts close and unused credits expire; the Canva replacement needs a Canva account, and Canva’s remover has historically been a Pro feature. This tool stays standalone, free and sign-up-free.

Can I make a passport photo with a white background?+

Yes — remove the background, choose the white preset, and use the Passport 35×45 crop chip before downloading. Always check your country’s official photo rules first, since some authorities restrict digitally altered photos.

Why does the first image take longer than the rest?+

On first use your browser downloads the AI model (about 44 MB) and caches it for next time. After that, a removal typically takes a few seconds per image, depending on your device.

Which formats can I open and download?+

Open JPG, PNG, WebP and anything else your browser can display. Download as a transparent PNG, or flattened on your chosen background as PNG or JPG. Batch mode exports transparent PNGs, individually or as one ZIP.

Can I remove the background from a photo without signing up?+

Yes. The remover works entirely in your browser with no account, no signup and no upload to a server — open the page, drop in your photo, and download the result.

How do I make a logo background transparent for my website?+

Upload your logo image, remove the background, and download it as a transparent PNG. For crisp edges on small logos, use a high-resolution source file and zoom in to check fine details before downloading.

Does the background remover work for product photos for Amazon or Daraz?+

Yes. Use the product-photo preset to get a clean white background that meets marketplace listing requirements. Shoot on a plain surface with even lighting for the best automatic cut-out, then download at full resolution.

Can I remove backgrounds from group photos or photos with several people at once?+

Yes — the model handles several people in one photo in a single pass, no need to cut them out one by one. Hair and edges are a strength of RMBG-1.4: it is trained on fine detail, so most hair, fur and flyaway strands are kept cleanly. Very wispy strands against a busy or similarly coloured background can soften slightly — a little Edge softness in the editor usually blends them in naturally.

Can I process several images in one session, one after another, without signing up?+

Yes — there is no account and no per-session limit. Use “Start over with a new image” to work through photos one by one, or use Batch mode to process several at once and download them as individual PNGs or one ZIP. The AI model loads once and is reused for every image in the session.

What resolution and file size do full-resolution downloads keep — and is a transparent PNG or a white background better for printing?+

Downloads keep your image’s original resolution (up to 5000 px on the longest side) — nothing is downscaled. File size depends on the photo: a large transparent PNG can be several MB, while a JPG flattened on a background is much smaller. For printing, choose the white background: paper has no transparency, so a transparent PNG prints as white anyway, and print shops handle flattened files more predictably. Keep the transparent PNG for screens, listings and design work.

How do I get clean edges around hair and fur — and what if strands look cut off?+

Start with the photo itself: hair and fur cut out cleanest when the subject stands out from the background — a plain, contrasting backdrop, even lighting and a sharp, in-focus shot give the model the most edge detail to work with. In the editor, use the Edge softness slider sparingly: a little (around 1 px) blends wispy strands in naturally, while too much eats fine detail. If strands look cut off or missing, they usually blended into a similarly coloured or busy background in the original. Try a version of the photo with more contrast between subject and backdrop, lower the Edge softness to 0 and re-run, then zoom in on the preview to check the outline before downloading.

Should I download a transparent PNG or a JPG on a white background?+

Download the transparent PNG when the cut-out needs to sit on top of something else: logos on a website, stickers, video and stream overlays, thumbnails and any design work — PNG keeps the transparent (alpha) channel, and JPG cannot. Download the JPG on a white background when the image is finished as it is: printing, documents, application forms and ID-style photos, where paper and forms have no transparency and a smaller, flattened file is easier to share and upload. Rule of thumb: PNG if you will place it over something later, white JPG if it is the final picture.

What happens if my photo is very small or low quality?+

Your result keeps the resolution of the photo you started with — the tool never downscales, but it does not upscale or invent detail either, so a 400 px photo comes back at 400 px. Very small, blurry or heavily compressed photos also give softer, less certain edges, because there is less detail for the model to trace, and blocky compression artefacts around the subject can survive into the cut-out. For the best result, use the largest, sharpest version of the photo you have — the original from your camera or phone rather than a screenshot or a copy saved from a chat app.

Does the remover work on screenshots and scanned documents, or only on camera photos?+

It works on screenshots and scanned images too — not only camera photos. Anything your browser can open (JPG, PNG, WebP and similar) can be processed, including a screenshot with a clear subject, a scanned photo, a scanned signature or logo, or a screenshot of a product. Results are best when there is one clear foreground subject standing out from what is behind it. It is less suited to a full page of text: the model looks for a subject to keep, so faint pencil, pale ink or fine lines on a scanned document can soften or drop out. For scans, use the highest-resolution scan you have, check the preview closely, and download the transparent PNG so you can place it on white again if needed.

How do I keep a natural-looking shadow under the subject after removing the background?+

In most photos you cannot keep the original shadow exactly as it was: a cast shadow sits on the floor or surface, so the model usually removes it along with the background. A little Edge softness (around 1 px) helps the base of the subject blend in so it does not look cut out, but it will not recreate a shadow. For the most natural result, download the transparent PNG and add a soft shadow in your photo or design editor — a dark, heavily blurred shape or drop shadow directly under the subject, at low opacity, shifted slightly away from the light source. Keep it tight under feet, wheels or the product base rather than floating around the whole outline. If the original setting matters, the Blur original background option keeps the scene — and its real shadow — visible behind the subject instead.

What file size or resolution works best as a source image for a clean cutout?+

Aim for the original file at roughly 1,500 to 4,000 px on the longest side — large enough for the model to trace hair, fur and fine edges, and within this tool's 5,000 px maximum. File size on its own matters less than sharpness and compression: a clean 2–5 MB JPG or PNG from your phone or camera will usually cut out better than a much larger but blurry file. Avoid copies that have been shrunk or heavily recompressed by chat and social apps, and avoid enlarging a small image before uploading it — that adds file size without adding real edge detail. If you have a choice, pick the sharpest, least-compressed version and let the tool return it at its original resolution.

Can I use the remover for passport, ID-style and official document photos?+

Yes — you can use it to prepare a photo with a plain background for passport, ID and other official document applications, but this tool cannot guarantee acceptance. For the best chance, start with a recent head-and-shoulders photo facing the camera, use a plain background with even lighting and no shadows on your face or behind you, and follow your authority's rules on size, expression and head coverings. Always check the issuing authority's current photo requirements before submitting, because final acceptance is always the issuing authority's decision, not this tool's.

How can I get a clean result when removing a background from a busy or cluttered photo?+

You can, but plain backgrounds usually give cleaner edges because the model can clearly separate the subject from what is behind it — busy patterns, overlapping objects and similar colours make edges harder to trace. If your background is busy, use the largest, sharpest version of the photo you have, choose a version where the subject has higher contrast against the background, and use bright, even lighting so hair and outlines are well defined. Zoom in on the preview to check edges, and a little Edge softness (around 1 px) can help the cut-out blend more naturally.

For privacy, do my photos leave my device?+

No. The tool runs 100% in your browser, so your photos are processed locally on your own device and are never uploaded to a server. The AI model is downloaded once to your browser and cached, but the images you open, edit and download stay on your device — nothing is sent, stored or shared by this tool.

Can I change the background to a different colour after removing the original?+

Yes. Once the original background is removed, pick any preset swatch — white, black, light grey, ID blue, red or green screen — or use the Custom color picker to set any colour you like, and your cut-out is flattened onto it when you download. Practical tip: choose a colour that contrasts with your subject's clothing or product colour, so the outline stays crisp and clearly defined.

Can I remove the background from a photo taken in low light?+

Yes, the model can cut out subjects from dim or evening photos, although edges are less certain where a dark subject blends into a dark background. Practical tip: brighten a copy of the photo slightly before uploading it and keep Edge softness around 1 px, then zoom in on the preview to check hair and outlines before downloading.

Can I replace the removed background with a photo of my own?+

Yes. After removing the original background, choose the Own photo option in the New background controls and pick any image from your device — a room, a landscape or a studio backdrop — and your subject is placed over it. Practical tip: pick a replacement photo with lighting and colours similar to your subject's, so the combined picture looks natural rather than pasted in.

Can I use the background remover to make cutouts for YouTube thumbnails and social media posts?+

Yes — this is one of its best uses. Remove the background and download the transparent PNG, then drop the cut-out onto your thumbnail or post design in any editor so you can add bold text, colours and graphics behind you. For thumbnails, start with a large, expressive, well-lit photo and check the edges at full size before exporting, and for social posts use the Square 1:1 or 4:5 crop chips to frame the cut-out for the feed.

Does it work on old scanned family photos with faded or damaged backgrounds?+

Yes, it works on scanned family photos, and faded backgrounds often cut out cleanly because the people still stand out from what is behind them. For the best result, scan at the highest resolution you can (300–600 dpi), save as JPG or PNG, and use a copy with slightly boosted contrast if the whole print has faded evenly. Note that it only removes the background — scratches, tears or stains on the people themselves will remain, so repair those in a photo editor afterwards if needed.

How does it handle semi-transparent things like glass, veils or sheer fabric?+

It attempts to keep semi-transparent subjects like drinking glasses, windows, bridal veils and sheer curtains, but results vary more than with solid subjects — very sheer areas can come out partly transparent, patchy or more solid than in the original, because the model has to decide how see-through each pixel is. Results are cleanest when the glass or fabric contrasts with what is behind it and is sharply in focus. Check the preview on both the checkerboard and a solid dark and light background before downloading, and keep Edge softness low (0–1 px) so fine sheer edges are not softened away.

Can I turn a photo cutout into a WhatsApp sticker?+

Yes — remove the background here and download the transparent PNG, then bring that PNG into WhatsApp's sticker maker or a sticker-pack app to save it as a sticker. Practical tip: use the Trim empty edges option and the Square 1:1 crop before downloading, so the subject fills the sticker frame instead of sitting small in a corner.

Can I remove the background from food photos for a restaurant menu or food-delivery listing?+

Yes — cut out the dish and download it as a transparent PNG for your own menu design, or flattened on white or a solid brand colour for a clean, consistent delivery-listing look across every dish. Practical tip: photograph each dish from the same angle in even light and let steam settle first, since steam and harsh shadows soften the plate's edges and make the set look uneven.

Can I remove the background from real-estate or property listing photos?+

Yes, for the marketing around a listing — for example cutting out a house exterior for a flyer or social post, or making a clean agent headshot with a solid background for a listing page. Use it on presentation only and never to change what the property itself looks like, since listing photos must represent the property honestly. Practical tip: for exterior shots, place the cut-out on a plain light background rather than a different location photo, so the house stays the clear, truthful focus of the image.

Can I remove the background from a photo of my car to sell it online?+

Yes — a clean cutout on a plain background makes listings on OLX, Facebook Marketplace or PakWheels look professional. Shoot in daylight against an uncluttered wall, keep the whole car in frame, then remove the background and place it on white or light grey. Practical tip: wash the car first — dirt and dust show up clearly once the background is gone.

Does it work on shiny products like jewellery, watches or glass bottles?+

Yes for most — reflections and shine stay on the product itself while the background is cut away. For very reflective items, use soft daylight and avoid a mirror-like surface behind the item, since strong reflections of the room can confuse the edge detection. Practical tip: photograph shiny items on a plain matte surface rather than glass or chrome.

Can I remove the background from a signature or hand-drawn logo on white paper?+

Yes — scan or photograph the signature or logo on plain white paper in good light, remove the white background to get a transparent PNG, then use it as a watermark or letterhead logo. Keep the original scan at high resolution so thin pen strokes stay sharp. Practical tip: use a dark pen on clean white paper — pencil or light ink leaves faint edges.

Can I remove the background from a pet photo — will the fur and whiskers survive?+

Yes — the model is trained on fine detail, so most fur and whiskers around the edges are kept cleanly in the cut-out. For the cleanest result, use a clear, well-lit photo of your pet taken against a plain background: the stronger the contrast between the fur and what is behind it, the more edge detail the model has to trace and the fewer stray strands get lost.

Can I remove the background from wedding or event invitation photos?+

Yes — cut out a couple portrait for an invite card, or lift a venue or detail shot onto your invitation design, then download the transparent PNG to place in any layout. And because the tool runs 100% in your browser, those personal photos are never uploaded to a server, so your wedding and event pictures stay private on your own device.

Can I remove the background from a professional headshot for LinkedIn or a job profile?+

Yes — remove the original background and place your headshot on a clean plain colour or an office-style backdrop photo for a polished job-profile look. You can also download the transparent PNG, so the same cut-out can be reused on a CV, a company website or any other profile without redoing the work.
